newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-SECURITIES WATCH-DOG LINE-UP IN TWO WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-SECURITIES WATCH-DOG LINE-UP IN TWO WEEKS.

text.p: The securities commission said on Friday that it expects the final line-up of its board, adding three more names to the current four, to be decided by parliament in two weeks time.
"We expect the remaining three board members to be approved by parliament within two weeks," Talis Laizans, deputy chairman of the commission, told Reuters.
The securities commission will will act as the state watch-dog of the country's securities market.
Parliament on Thursday approved two candidates: Viktor Shadinov, the legal director of the privatisation agency, and Andris Klauss, an economics professor.
"The board is almost ready to begin its functions, with four members in place," Laizans said.
The board already consists of chairman Viktors Gustsons and deputy chairman Talis Laizans.
Parliament earlier rejected two of the five board candidates suggested by the commission, Ojars Kehris and Guntis Urlovskis while Ilmar Rimshevics, central bank deputy president, withdrew his name.

Ojars Kehris currently holds a number of high posts including board posts with Vetspils Nafta oil terminal and oil transit company Latrostrans. Guntis Urlovskis is finance director of the Turiba consumer union association.
